Commentary.Commentary: Right then, that is it from the game. It was the rain gods who came out to be victorious. The 2nd ODI between these sides will take place on Saturday, the 23rd of September. The game begins at 1.30 pm IST (8 am GMT). Do join us a bit early for the build-up as well. Until then, take care, and cheers!

Bangladesh bowlers were excellent. Mustafizur Rahman picked up a three-fer and Nasum Ahmed chipped in with two wickets. It took a while for them to break the Young-Nicholls stand but they made sure it was well done. The rest of the bowles were wicketless.

So, the inevitable has happened and the game has been CALLED OFF. The Kiwis will be happy though as they seemed to be in some trouble. They had a shaky start but Young and Nicholls steadied the ship. The former fell for 58 while Nicholls fell for just six runs shy off his half century.
Well, it is coming down pretty heavy now and chances of any kind of game looks bleak. Fingers crossed though.

It's raining again. We don't think New Zealand will bat again. To recap the innings, for New Zealand it was just about one big partnership in the middle phase. They didn't start well but Young and Henry Nicholls did well to steady the ship. However, just when they were trying to change the gears, Mustafizur Rahman came back for his second spell and broke the partnership. On the other side, the spinners got a good amount of purchase and it was Nasum Ahmed who made the most of it. He took two wickets but it was Rahman with three who made the big difference. The innings were filled with rain interruptions as well. Stay tuned.

Update - 6.29 pm IST (12.59 pm GMT) - The rain has stopped and the groundsmen are removing the covers. We should have the resumption shortly. The good thing is we haven't lost anymore overs. And, just as we type the covers are back on as the rain has arrived.
Update - 6.10 pm IST (12.40 pm GMT) - Well, it has started to rain again and the covers are back on. Let's hope it is a passing shower. Stay tuned.

Hello and welcome everyone! A new ODI series kicks off as we see the Kiwis take on Bangladesh. Ferguson is all set to lead his inexperienced team against the Bangladeshi side who are facing a lot of criticism after their disappointing exit from the Asia Cup. The seam goes for New Zealand who faced an heavy defeat from the hands of England recently. With the World Cup next, there is lot to look forward in this series. Stay tuned for toss and other updates.
... MATCH DAY ...

Hello folks. We are awaiting an exciting ODI series as the New Zealand team arrives in Bangladesh to play 3 matches before the World Cup campaign begins for both teams. The 1st ODI will be played in the capital city, Dhaka. New Zealand are arriving into this series after facing a loss against England. They will hope to win this to gain a lot of confidence ahead of a very important World Cup coming up to be played in similar conditions. The team will be led by their pacer, Lockie Ferguson along with the experienced Trent Boult by his side. After facing a series defeat by 3-1 against England, they should hope that their main players get back in form and get used to the playing conditions in the sub-continent. Their batting is proving to be on the weaker side. Their bowling unit is in better shape. New Zealand will try hard to start off the series with a win to boost their confidence. Bangladesh is having the same story and is on the road to making a comeback after a very bad Asia Cup campaign. The team did not perform as expected and were out of the Super 4 after they lost 2 matches. However, they ended their campaign on a high after clinching a win against India in the last league match of the tournament. They have the home advantage in this series and will hope to exploit the advantage. Litton Das will be leading the team for the first 2 matches. The youngster, Tanzim Hasan Sakib, who performed exceptionally well in his debut game against India is also included in the squad. Some of these players will also be playing in the World Cup in India at the start of next month. They will look to dominate this series and boost their morale ahead of the tournament.  The first match will be an important one to gain a significant one to gain a lead in this series. Which team are you supporting?
